legacy_inventory.local_acceptance_note: All 40 source leads now have final source-reference or disposition notes under documents/references/. Thirty-six official external references are usable only within their recorded scopes; four leads are not accepted or remain pending verification. The 31 converted candidate files and captured inputs remain in the EU Source Update Monitor local-only archive. No local source text, topic coverage, or country completion is accepted.

policy: A human-reviewed official link is usable for ordinary research within the identified publisher, instrument, language, displayed date or cutoff, reviewed content, and limitations. Slov-Lex, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Ministry of Interior are clearly identifiable official government sources. Use their government-published current or date-bound versions directly. No Gazette-fragment reconstruction, local capture, hash, replay, conversion, API access, or copying permission is required for link use. Check a later amendment only when it may materially affect the issue. Link acceptance is separate from local-copy acceptance, topic coverage, and country completion.

sk_02.publisher: Slov-Lex, electronic Collection of Laws of the Slovak Republic
sk_02.version_or_cutoff: Version effective from 1 October 2026; Slov-Lex history page showed it as the current open-ended version.
sk_02.scope: Act 404/2011 on Residence of Foreigners, including entry, residence, residence documents, removal, and EU-family provisions.
sk_02.reviewed_content: The official act history and binding PDF identify the act, version, and effective date. The act is a broad immigration statute and only a partial functional match for Directive 2004/38. Its general member-state definition includes EU, EEA, and Swiss states, while §§30 and 51–57 narrow the term to EU Member States.
limitations: The EEA, Swiss, EU, Slovak-return, and UK Withdrawal Agreement routes must be kept distinct where the act or another instrument does not expressly group them.
No article-by-article coverage or procedural completeness finding is made; see the coverage register.
The link does not accept a locally converted copy.

sk-minv-eu-registration-faq-2025.reviewed_content: The three-page official PDF was opened directly. It states the registration timing and personal police filing route, lists evidence by residence purpose, describes individual assessment of resources, and gives certificate/card issue steps.
limitations: This is March 2025 guidance, not a current checklist. For a present-day application, check Act 404/2011 in its version effective from 1 October 2026 and the current official Ministry instructions; later material changes may alter procedures or evidence.
The FAQ concerns EU-citizen residence registration and mentions family evidence in that context; it does not map all third-country family-member, extended-family, return, EEA or Swiss routes.
This accepts the official dated link only; it does not accept a local PDF copy, establish legal correctness after the stated date, or complete a topic.

human_review_site_offers.site_name: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs — Slovak diplomatic representations
human_review_site_offers.offer: Offer the official MZV mission directory and linked mission websites as a whole-site human review source for current visa and consular practice. The central pages and directory are usable as scoped official references, but local missions may set different checklists, appointments, submission channels, and outsourcing arrangements. Older pages found in the same official network are visibly stale and should not be treated as current rules.
human_review_site_offers.review_scope: For relevant applicant locations, identify the competent mission, current EU-family instructions, required documents, fee exemptions, appointment route, provider or outsourcing arrangement, and current forms. Record the page's date or version evidence and retain any inaccessible route as a human-review offer; do not infer that one mission's practice applies network-wide.
